He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]]. ==Early life== Robinson grew up in [[Manassas, Virginia]]. As a child, his family held season tickets for the [[Washington Wizards]]. He originally attended [[Montrose Christian School]] in [[Rockville, Maryland]], playing basketball mostly as a reserve player and was a teammate of future NBA player [[Justin Anderson (basketball)|Justin Anderson]]. He transferred to [[St. James School, Maryland]] before his junior year following the resignation of Montrose Christian's head coach, Stu Vetter. He immediately became a starter at St. James and averaged 13 points and six assists per game in his junior season. As a senior, Robinson averaged 21.8 points, 7.7 assists, 4.3 rebounds and 2.2 steals per game and was named the [[Washington County, Maryland|Washington County]] Player of the Year, Gatorade Maryland Boys Basketball Player of the Year, and a [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldmailmedia.com/sports/all-county-boys-basketball-saint-james-robinson-made-winning-his/article_c23c8fd8-3566-5b7e-8dc0-1bd6c0597974.html|title=All-County boys basketball: Saint James' Robinson made winning his specialty|first=Tim|last=Koelble|work=[[The Herald-Mail]]|date=March 28, 2015|access-date=July 15, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.insidenova.com/sports/prince_william/as-he-prepares-for-the-nba-draft-manassas-resident-justin/article_e79304c2-8d27-11e9-b668-8fa3763dbf0b.html|title=As he prepares for the NBA Draft, Manassas resident Justin Robinson is always one step ahead|website=InsideNoVa.com|first=David|last=Fawcett|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=July 15, 2019}} He was rated a three-star recruit by [[ESPN]], [[247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com]] and committed to play [[college basketball]] at Virginia Tech over offers from [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels|UNLV]] and [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]].{{cite web|url=https://fightinggobbler.com/2014/10/12/3-star-pg-justin-robinson-commits-virginia-tech-hokies/|title=3-Star PG Justin Robinson Commits to the Virginia Tech Hokies|first=Tim|last=Thomas|website=FightingGobbler.com|publisher=[[FanSided]]|date=October 12, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:Justin Robinson Virginia Tech (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Robinson in 2017]] Robinson played four seasons for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]]. He entered the starting lineup during his freshman season, averaging 7.3 points and 2.8 assists per game in 35 games (19 starts).{{cite web|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2016/10/31/virginia-tech-basketball-hokies-make-first-ncaa-tourney-since-2007/2/|title=Virginia Tech Basketball: Hokies to make first NCAA Tourney since 2007?|first=Carmine|last=Carcieri|website=BustingBrackets.com|publisher=[[FanSided]]|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2019|archive-date=July 16, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190716003440/https://bustingbrackets.com/2016/10/31/virginia-tech-basketball-hokies-make-first-ncaa-tourney-since-2007/2/|url-status=dead}} In his first full season as a sophomore, Robinson averaged 10.4 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.2 assist per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/virginia-tech-record-breaker-justin-robinson-masters-the-art-of/article_1e2bc5cc-7682-5fd1-8075-8b161617c1ae.html|title=Virginia Tech record-breaker Justin Robinson masters the art of the assist|first=Mark|last=Berman|work=[[The Roanoke Times]]|date=January 29, 2019|access-date=July 15, 2019}} As a junior, Robinson averaged 14 points and 5.6 assists (tied for second in the conference) and was named second team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]].{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2018/10/24/players-relish-virginia-virginia-tech-basketball-rivalry-rankings-or-not/?noredirect=on|title=Players relish Virginia-Virginia Tech basketball rivalry, rankings or not|first=Gene|last=Wang|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=October 24, 2018|access-date=July 15, 2019}} He averaged 13.5 points, 5.0 assists, and 3.2 rebounds while shooting 41.8% from three in 24 games in his senior season, missing 12 games due to a foot injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/07/wizards-sign-justin-robinson.html|title=Wizards Sign Justin Robinson|first=Luke|last=Adams|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 15, 2019}} He was named the ACC Player of the Week on January 28, 2019, after scoring 35 points with eight assists in a 78–56 win over [[2018–19 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wsls.com/sports/college-basketball/hokies-robinson-is-acc-player-of-the-week|title=Hokies' Robinson is ACC player of the week|first=John|last=Appicello|website=[[WSLS-TV|WSLS.com]]|date=January 28, 2019|access-date=July 16, 2019}} Robinson finished his career with 1,383 career points and a school-record 562 assists. He participated in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]] following his senior season, averaging 7.7 points and six assists in three games played.{{cite web|url=https://www.dailypress.com/sports/dp-spt-pit-justin-robinson-0418-story.html|title=Tech's Justin Robinson delivers in the clutch at PIT|first=Dave|last=Johnson|work=[[Daily Press (Virginia)|Daily Press]]|date=April 17, 2019|access-date=July 15, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2019–2020)=== [[File:2019 Justin Robinson (48824169206).jpg|thumb|left|Robinson season ticket holder, now playing for his childhood team|first=Chase|last=Hughes|website=[[NBC Sports Washington]]|date=July 7, 2019|access-date=July 15, 2019}} On October 23, 2019, Robinson made his debut in NBA, coming off from bench in a 100–108 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160631|title=Doncic-Porzingis debut carries Mavs past Wizards, 108-100|date=October 23, 2019|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=October 23, 2019}} Robinson averaged 1.4 points per game in nine games. Robinson was waived by the Wizards on January 5, 2020.{{cite web|title=Wizards waive Justin Robinson|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-justin-robinson-1-5-19|date=January 5, four rebounds and three assists over 33 minutes in a loss to the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite news |title=Justin Robinson: Scores 22 in loss 2020}} On December 7, he was waived by the 76ers.{{cite tweet |user=sixers |number=1336071738967220225 |date=December 7, 2020 |title=We have waived Lamine Diane and Justin Robinson.}} Robinson later 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=January 14, 2021}} In 13 games, he averaged 5.5 points, 3.4 rebounds, 5.9 assists and 1.62 steals in 31.1 minutes while shooting 40.5 percent from three point range, helping the Blue Coats reach the [[NBA G League]] Final.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Justin Robinson to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/robinson-210405|date=April 5,
